clue.text: Part of foot that may be painful in dance

definitions.text: Part of foot that may be painful

blocks.clueFragment: Part of foot that may be painful
blocks.note: first meaning: the padded area under the toes, which can ache
second meaning: a formal dancing party

explanation.surface: A dancer complains that one part of the foot hurts during the dance.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface links the two meanings as cause and effect, but they are separate senses of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The cushion beneath the toes is called this, and so is a grand formal social gathering for dancing.

clue.text: Flip ingredient in pub one's unable to choose?

definitions.note: a noun phrase from the proverb 'beggars can't be choosers'

indicators.note: one thing being in another means it sits inside it

blocks.note: a flip is a drink made with beaten egg

explanation.surface: Someone at the pub looks at a cocktail recipe and cannot decide what to put in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flip' reads as a verb, but it is an old drink made with beaten egg.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says beggars can't be choosers, so a beggar is someone with no choice.

clue.text: Waters rising, hence state of anxiety

indicators.note: in a down clue something rising is read from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: to water a plant is to wet it

explanation.surface: Floodwaters climb, so people become worried.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Waters' looks like a noun but is the verb, meaning wets.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in a stew is an idiom for being agitated or worried.

clue.text: Kindly include head of government in African country

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter
to include something is to take it inside

blocks.note: Benin is a West African state
the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: An instruction to put a gentle leader at the top of an African nation's government.
explanation.walkthrough: G goes inside BENIN: BENI-G-N. 'Kindly' looks like a polite 'please'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both adjectives describe a gentle, well-meaning and favourable disposition.

clue.text: Only Conservative is above criticism, ultimately, for bad behaviour

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so the final letter is taken

blocks.note: the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A political claim that only the Tory party is beyond reproach for misconduct.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'above' means placed before. A solecism is strictly a breach of grammar or etiquette.
explanation.definitionFit: A solecism is a breach of good manners or etiquette, a social blunder, hence improper conduct.

clue.text: Get marine redeployed on left of colonel's men

definitions.note: adjectival sense: belonging to a regiment

indicators.note: troops redeployed are moved into new positions, so the letters take a new order

explanation.surface: An order to move a marine to the left flank of a colonel's troops.
explanation.definitionFit: A colonel commands a regiment, and its soldiers are the men belonging to that military unit.

clue.text: A whistle-blower singularly shod? Not so

indicators.note: to be shod is to have one's foot inside footwear

blocks.note: single item of footwear: one boot rather than a pair

explanation.surface: Is a referee wearing just one boot properly shod? No.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not so' negates the 'shod' just before it, so the definition means unshod. 'Whistle-blower' suggests an informer, but here it is the match official.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone not wearing shoes has nothing on the feet, which is the meaning of the answer.

clue.text: For remote settlement, excel in sending mail?

definitions.note: a jokey verb: to out-post someone

blocks.note: first meaning: a distant station or colony
second meaning, whimsical: beat someone at posting letters

explanation.surface: A remote village is praised for its efficient postal service.
explanation.walkthrough: The second meaning is invented: the prefix OUT- means surpass, as in outrun, and POST means send letters; the question mark flags the coinage.
explanation.definitionFit: A distant frontier station or small settlement far from the centre is an outpost.

clue.text: European was bounder, ran for union without approval

blocks.note: to lope is to run with long bounding strides

explanation.surface: A disreputable European cad ran off to marry without family blessing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bounder' suggests a cad, but here it is something that bounds along.
explanation.definitionFit: Eloping means running away secretly to marry, without parental consent.

clue.text: Steps up attempt to escape

blocks.note: first meaning: a staircase, a run of stairs

explanation.surface: Someone intensifies a bid to get away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Steps up' reads as a verb meaning intensifies, but it is the stairs leading upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A flight of stairs is a set of steps; taking flight means running away.

clue.text: We are prone to absorb blow as harmless deception

indicators.note: something absorbed is taken in and held inside

blocks.note: to lie is to be prone, lying flat

explanation.surface: People admitting they tend to take a punch by way of innocent pretence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prone' reads as 'inclined to', but here means lying flat.
explanation.definitionFit: A white lie is a small untruth told to be kind, a deceit that does no harm.

clue.text: Disorderly march cancelled — is even changing into friendly campaign

indicators.note: something disorderly is out of its proper arrangement
these letters are changing their places

blocks.note: an event that is called off is cancelled

explanation.surface: An unruly protest march is scrapped and becomes a goodwill effort instead.
explanation.definitionFit: A charm offensive is a deliberate drive to win people over by being pleasant.

clue.text: Women having fun with jolly fellows around new piano

indicators.note: around means surrounding, holding the next part inside

explanation.surface: Women enjoy themselves with cheerful men gathered round a new piano.
explanation.walkthrough: N P goes inside HE-ARTIES. A hen party is a British name for a bachelorette party.
explanation.definitionFit: A hen party is a pre-wedding celebration for women, so such gatherings are groups of women celebrating.

clue.text: Mainly overlook how to make money illegally

indicators.note: mainly means most but not all, so the final letter is dropped

explanation.surface: Advice that mostly ignoring the rules is the way to earn money criminally.
explanation.definitionFit: To forge banknotes is to counterfeit currency, producing cash unlawfully.

clue.text: Shot in game

blocks.note: second meaning: a children's card game

explanation.surface: A shot played during a match.
explanation.walkthrough: Snap is a simple card game in which players call out when two matching cards appear.
explanation.definitionFit: A snapshot is a casual photograph, and the card game has the same name.

clue.text: Manipulation of figures elevated favourite — be curious about it

indicators.note: about means going round, enclosing the rest

blocks.note: to pry is to be nosy

explanation.surface: Someone suspects a promoted favourite of cooking the books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Manipulation of figures' suggests fiddling accounts; the figures are puppets.
explanation.definitionFit: Puppetry is the art of working puppets, small figures moved by strings or hands.

clue.text: Disconcerted ruler in the West

indicators.note: in means placed inside the following word

blocks.note: R for rex or regina, king or queen

explanation.surface: A monarch in the West has been unsettled.
explanation.walkthrough: R goes inside THE, then W follows. The definition is a past-tense verb: something threw you.
explanation.definitionFit: To throw someone is to confuse or unsettle them, so threw is a past tense of disconcert.

clue.text: Western criminal paid to kill American poet

explanation.surface: A cowboy-film outlaw hired to murder an American poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Western' suggests a cowboy film; it only supplies one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Walt Whitman, author of Leaves of Grass, is a celebrated nineteenth-century US poet.

clue.text: Little child's great strength, as you can hear

indicators.note: what you can hear is the spoken sound, not the spelling

explanation.surface: Remarking that a small child is remarkably strong.
explanation.definitionFit: Mite is an affectionate word for a small child, used for a tiny creature.

clue.text: How pieces of chintz are ordered — or almost!

definitions.text: How pieces of chintz are ordered — or almost!

blocks.clueFragment: How pieces of chintz are ordered
blocks.note: surface reading: how a shop stocks lengths of patterned cloth
setter's reading: the letters of both chintz and almost each run in dictionary order

explanation.surface: A query about how a draper arranges cloth samples.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces are letters: C, H, I, N, T, Z already follow A-to-Z order, and so do A, L, M, O, S, T.
explanation.definitionFit: Letters in A-to-Z sequence are arranged in the order of the abc.

clue.text: Surrounded by diamonds, in a haze

indicators.note: in means placed inside what follows

explanation.surface: Someone dazzled by diamonds, in a dreamy daze.
explanation.walkthrough: D goes inside A MIST: A-MI-D-ST.
explanation.definitionFit: Amidst is a preposition meaning in the middle of, with things all around.

clue.text: Showing lots of energy against English after start of play

blocks.note: Act I, the opening act of a drama

explanation.surface: A team plays with vigour against England after the first whistle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Play' suggests sport, but it is a stage play, which begins with Act I.
explanation.definitionFit: Active means lively and energetic, always on the go.

clue.text: Foreign citizen producing articles about part of UK

indicators.note: about means placed round something else

blocks.note: the articles A, THE and AN

explanation.surface: An overseas national writing pieces about a region of Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Articles' suggests newspaper pieces; it means the grammatical articles, with Northern Ireland placed between the last two.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Athens is a citizen of the Greek capital, foreign from a British viewpoint.

clue.text: Alternative responses to request for secluded place

explanation.surface: Different answers given to someone asking for a private spot.
explanation.walkthrough: The two replies are refusal and agreement, set side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: A nook is a sheltered corner or recess, a quiet hidden spot.

clue.text: Stuff that's less shiny?

blocks.note: second meaning: the comparative of matt, a dull finish

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is read as MATT-ER, more matt; the question mark flags the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Matter is material substance, and a matt surface is dull, so a duller one is comparatively matter.

clue.text: Noble, sooner than should be the case, ending like that

indicators.note: the word's own end comes too soon, as its meaning says, so its tail is cut

blocks.clueFragment: sooner than should be the case
blocks.note: early means before the due time

explanation.surface: An aristocrat arrives prematurely and leaves the same way.
explanation.walkthrough: The word for premature is itself ended prematurely, losing its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An earl is a British nobleman ranking below a marquess.

clue.text: Rubbish removed from seaside briskly

indicators.note: the letters are taken out from within the next words

blocks.note: the run of letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: Litter is cleared quickly from the beach.
explanation.definitionFit: Debris is scattered waste and fragments, a synonym of litter or refuse.

clue.text: Moron I've confused who will swallow anything?

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase for a noun: one who eats anything

indicators.note: something confused is muddled out of order

explanation.surface: An insult: a muddled idiot who believes any story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swallow anything' suggests gullibility; literally it is eating any food.
explanation.definitionFit: An omnivore eats both plants and animals, so its diet excludes almost nothing.
